account: NICE notes that missed fractures are reported to be the most common diagnostic error in emergency departments. The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) assessed AI software that marks suspected fractures on X-rays for the clinician who reads them. Its external assessment group found 16 eligible studies, most of them on BoneView and RBfracture. In these studies, clinicians who read with the software detected more fractures without a loss of specificity. In a BoneView study of emergency physicians, sensitivity rose from 61% to 74%. RBfracture raised it from 74% to 83%, and Rayvolve from 79% to 94%. In guidance published on 14 January 2025, the committee concluded that the evidence suggests that these technologies have the potential to improve fracture detection, and it allowed Rayvolve, TechCare Alert, BoneView and RBfracture in NHS urgent care while more evidence is generated. Most studies were retrospective case-control reader studies, none took place in UK urgent care, and reading times changed by only a few seconds. The committee noted that unassisted readers were less accurate than expected, so the gain may be overstated.
